title: Elon Lindenstrauss, a mathematician from Jerusalem, was the first Israeli to win the Fields Medal

trailer.text: Elon Lindenstrauss, born in Jerusalem and a professor at the Einstein Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University, is the son of mathematician Yoram Lindenstrauss, winner of the Israel Prize for Mathematics.
On 19 August 2010 he received the Fields Medal in Hyderabad, India, and became the first Israeli to win it.
According to Israel21c, the medal is considered the equivalent of a Nobel Prize.
According to the International Mathematical Union, he received it for his results on measure rigidity in ergodic theory and their applications to number theory.
After years in Princeton he chose to continue at the Hebrew University, and according to Israel21c the primary reason he cites is family.

stations.title: A child from Jerusalem, from a family of mathematicians

paragraphs.text: Elon Lindenstrauss was born in Jerusalem in 1970 to Naomi and Yoram Lindenstrauss.
His father, Prof. Joram Lindenstrauss, is a professor emeritus at the Einstein Institute, a winner of the Israel Prize for Mathematics and a member of the Israeli National Academy of Sciences.
Elon is thus a second-generation mathematician.
According to a ynet article from August 2010, his uncle was then State Comptroller Micha Lindenstrauss.
At 18 he represented Israel at the International Mathematical Olympiad and won a bronze medal.
He is a graduate of the Israel Air Force's Talpiot program, a reserve major in the Israel Defense Forces and a winner of the Israel Defense Prize.
According to Israel21c, he started out later than usual, because he volunteered for extra service.

According to the International Mathematical Union, he earned all his degrees at the Hebrew University: a B.Sc. in Mathematics and Physics in 1991, an M.Sc. in Mathematics in 1995, and a Ph.D. in 1999 on entropy properties of dynamical systems, under the supervision of Prof. Benjamin Weiss.

stations.title: Princeton, Stanford, and prizes along the way

paragraphs.text: According to Globes, Lindenstrauss was a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, an assistant professor at Stanford and a visiting member at the Courant Institute.
According to Princeton, he came to Princeton University in 2004.
He himself said that he had spent many years in Princeton, at various stages of his career.
According to Israel21c, he has published 35 papers since 1995.

According to the International Mathematical Union, he won the prize of the European Mathematical Society in 2004, and according to ynet he also won the 2009 Erdős Prize of the Israel Mathematical Union and the Fermat Prize for Mathematics of the Toulouse Mathematics Institute.
He also won the Salem Prize, but the sources disagree on the year.
According to the medal citation, Lindenstrauss developed extraordinarily powerful theoretical tools in ergodic theory, a field originally developed to understand celestial mechanics.
The field began in the 1930s, in the work of mathematicians including John von Neumann.
According to the International Mathematical Union, ergodic theory is the study of measure preserving transformations, and Lindenstrauss made far-reaching advances in it.
According to Ynet, Prof. Alex Lubotzky said the prize was given for work that uses probabilistic and dynamic systems to solve problems in number theory.
Together with Einsiedler and Katok, Lindenstrauss proved the Furstenberg and Margulis conjecture, under a further hypothesis of positive entropy.
According to the International Mathematical Union, he also resolved the arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak, in the theory of modular forms.
He is also known for applying ergodic theory to a longstanding problem in number theory, the Littlewood Conjecture.
According to Peter Sarnak, the problem is so difficult that everyone else who has tried it has come away empty-handed.
According to Israel21c, Lindenstrauss made strides in understanding the Littlewood Conjecture over ten years.
Efim Zelmanov said that Lindenstrauss works in an incredibly abstract and complicated area, even by the standards of mathematics.
Lindenstrauss himself said that he received the prize for a series of projects, some of them with partners, and that one of the joys is the ability to join forces with other mathematicians.

stations.title: A six-month secret, and a ceremony in India

paragraphs.text: Lindenstrauss said he had known about the prize for six months.
He was told to keep it a secret, and he did.
According to Arutz 7, he said he was surprised when he heard about the honor.
On 19 August 2010 he received the medal in Hyderabad, India.
This took place at the opening of the International Congress of Mathematicians, which the International Mathematical Union convenes every four years.
According to Princeton, the awards were presented on Thursday, at the opening ceremony of the congress.
The medal was presented to him by the president of India, Pratibha Patil.
That year three other laureates received the medal alongside Lindenstrauss.
According to Princeton, they were Cédric Villani, Ngo Bao Chau and Stanislav Smirnov.
According to Tablet, Israel was overrepresented at the congress among the lecturers invited to speak.
The Fields Medal was established by Canadian mathematician John Charles Fields and is named after him.
According to Princeton, it is awarded every four years to mathematicians up to the age of 40, and two to four can receive it each time.
According to Israel21c, it is considered the equivalent of a Nobel Prize.
On the question of who awards it, the sources disagree.
Lindenstrauss was the first Israeli to win it.
According to Tablet, this was the first time the medal had been awarded to an Israeli-born mathematician.
According to Tablet, it is surprising that the medal had eluded Israeli mathematicians until then, as a large proportion of its winners are of Jewish descent.
The president of the Hebrew University, Prof. Menachem Ben-Sasson, said that Israel is indeed a power in mathematics, but had not won the Fields Medal until then.
The medal comes with a cash prize, and on the amount, too, the sources disagree.
According to Globes, this is a relatively small sum compared with the Nobel Prize of a million dollars.
According to Globes, Prime Minister Netanyahu told Lindenstrauss that this is a great achievement for him and for the State of Israel, and that they are proud of him.
Prof. Alex Lubotzky said that Lindenstrauss received the medal for research that solved some of the most difficult and complex problems in number theory.
Lubotzky stressed that the work has a strong basis in methods developed by mathematicians at the Hebrew University.
Ben-Sasson said that people such as Lindenstrauss should be considered Israeli "cultural heroes."
He said that the age limit of 40 is an obstacle for young Israeli researchers, who begin their academic careers later because of military service.
According to ynet, Ben-Sasson said that Lindenstrauss proves that talented people can cope with this age barrier as well.
According to Peter Sarnak, Lindenstrauss is charming, very modest and a deep thinker.
Lindenstrauss himself told Ynet that the feeling is a little odd, and that he is not used to speaking to journalists.
According to Tablet, he declined to be interviewed for their article.
According to Israel21c, speaking from India the day after the ceremony, he said he still has much to accomplish professionally.
Lindenstrauss is married and the father of three children, and the family lives in Jerusalem.
According to Israel21c, family is the primary reason he cites for pursuing his career at the Hebrew University rather than in the United States.
He said that what made returning easier is that there is a wonderful mathematical community in Israel.
According to Globes, he told Netanyahu of the many temptations around the world for leading Israeli lecturers, and of his desire to stay at the Hebrew University in spite of them.
According to Tablet, many of the best choose to stay in Israel, despite offers from leading institutions abroad.
On the question of exactly when he joined the Hebrew University faculty, the sources say different things.
The Einstein Institute of Mathematics was founded in 1925, with the opening of the Hebrew University.
According to Lubotzky, in the two years before Lindenstrauss won the Fields Medal in 2010, five of the institute's researchers won European Union research grants.
Lubotzky said that despite the poor results of Israeli schoolchildren in international tests in recent years, Israel is still among the elite in outstanding mathematical research.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, הפרס הכספי הוא 15,000 דולר קנדי, שהם 14,460 דולר או 54,760 שקלים.
claims.quote: With a cash prize of 15,000 Canadian dollars ($14,460 or 54,760 shekels), it recognizes significant achievements as well as promising potential in mathematicians up to the age of 40.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, ראש הממשלה נתניהו אמר ללינדנשטראוס שזהו הישג גדול עבורו ועבור מדינת ישראל ושהם גאים בו.
claims.quote: This is a great achievement both for yourself and the State of Israel and we are proud of you.

claims.text: לפי פרופ' אלכס לובוצקי, לינדנשטראוס קיבל את המדליה על מחקרו שפתר כמה מהבעיות הקשות והמורכבות ביותר בתורת המספרים.
claims.quote: Prof. Lindenstrauss received the Fields Medal in recognition of his research solving some of the most difficult and complex problems in number theory.

claims.text: לובוצקי הדגיש שעבודתו של לינדנשטראוס נשענת היטב על שיטות שפיתחו מתמטיקאים באוניברסיטה העברית.
claims.quote: has a strong basis in methods developed by mathematicians at the Hebrew University.

claims.text: בן-ששון אמר שאנשים כמו לינדנשטראוס ראויים להיחשב "גיבורי תרבות" ישראליים.
claims.quote: He said that people such as Lindenstrauss should be considered Israeli "cultural heroes."

claims.text: בן-ששון אמר שמגבלת הגיל של 40 היא מכשול לחוקרים ישראלים צעירים, שמתחילים קריירה אקדמית מאוחר יותר בגלל השירות הצבאי.
claims.quote: The age limit of 40 for winning it is definitely an obstacle for young Israeli researchers who have to begin their academic careers later than others because of their military obligations,

claims.text: בן-ששון אמר ל-ynet שעד כה אף חוקר ישראלי לא זכה בפרס, אך לינדנשטראוס מוכיח שמוכשרים יכולים להתמודד גם עם מכשול גיל זה.
claims.quote: Israel is a mathematical power, but till now no Israeli researcher had won this prize,

claims.text: לפי סרנק, לינדנשטראוס מקסים, צנוע מאוד וחושב עמוק.
claims.quote: He is charming, a very modest guy and a very deep thinker.

claims.text: לינדנשטראוס אמר ל-ynet שההרגשה מוזרה מעט ושהוא לא רגיל לדבר עם עיתונאים.
claims.quote: The feeling is a little odd, I'm not used to speaking to journalists.

claims.text: לפי טאבלט, לינדנשטראוס סירב להתראיין לכתבה, והוא בנו של המתמטיקאי יורם לינדנשטראוס.
claims.quote: Fields Medal winner Lindenstrauss (who declined to be interviewed for this piece) is the son of mathematician Joram Lindenstrauss, an eminent figure in his own right.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, לינדנשטראוס אמר מהודו למחרת שעדיין יש לו הרבה מה להשיג מקצועית.
claims.quote: Speaking to ISRAEL21c from India the following day, the tired but elated mathematician says he still has much to accomplish professionally

claims.text: לינדנשטראוס נשוי ואב לשלושה ילדים, והמשפחה מתגוררת בירושלים.
claims.quote: He is married and the father of three children. The family lives in Jerusalem.

claims.text: לינדנשטראוס אמר שהקל עליו לחזור שיש בישראל קהילה מתמטית נפלאה.
claims.quote: What made it easier is that there is a wonderful mathematical community in Israel

claims.text: לפי גלובס, לינדנשטראוס סיפר לראש הממשלה נתניהו על הפיתויים הרבים בעולם למרצים ישראלים מובילים ועל רצונו להישאר באוניברסיטה העברית למרותם.
claims.quote: Prof. Lindenstrauss told Prime Minister Netanyahu of the many temptations around the world for leading Israeli lecturers and of his desire to stay at the Hebrew University in spite of them.

claims.text: לפי טאבלט, למרות הפיתוי של הצעות ממוסדות מובילים בחו"ל, רבים מהטובים ביותר בוחרים להישאר בישראל.
claims.quote: Notwithstanding the temptation of offers at leading institutions abroad, many of the best elect to stay in Israel.

claims.text: לינדנשטראוס הוא פרופסור באוניברסיטה העברית מאז 2008.
claims.quote: He has been a professor at the Hebrew University since 2008.

claims.text: המכון איינשטיין למתמטיקה באוניברסיטה העברית נוסד ב-1925, עם פתיחת האוניברסיטה.
claims.quote: The Einstein Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University was founded in 1925, concurrent with the opening of the university.

claims.text: לפי לובוצקי, בשנתיים האחרונות חמישה חוקרים מהמכון זכו במענקי מחקר של האיחוד האירופי.
claims.quote: In the last two years five of the institute's researchers won European Union scientific grants

claims.text: לובוצקי אמר שלמרות הישגים נמוכים של תלמידי ישראל במבחנים בינלאומיים בשנים האחרונות, ישראל עדיין בצמרת במחקר מתמטי מצטיין.
claims.quote: despite the fact that Israeli schoolchildren have ranked poorly in recent years in international tests in mathematics, Israel is still among the elite in outstanding mathematical research

claims.text: לפי האיגוד המתמטי הבינלאומי, לינדנשטראוס זכה בפרס החברה המתמטית האירופית ב-2004.
claims.quote: European Mathematical Society Prize 2004
